title: The fibre of Spec(T) -> Spec(R) over p is homeomorphic to Spec of the fibre ring
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to T$ be a ring map, $f:\operatorname{Spec}(T)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, $\mathfrak q\mapsto\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, the induced map of spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ a prime ideal with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then the fibre $f^{-1}(\mathfrak p)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(T)$, with the subspace topology, is homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$; a homeomorphism is given by sending a prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ to $j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$, where $j:T\to T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $t\mapsto t\otimes1$.

source.place: Algebra, Remark 00E6 (remark-fundamental-diagram, line 3422): on spectra the horizontal maps induce homeomorphisms onto their images and the squares induce fibre squares of topological spaces
